To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) hand-object interaction is beneficial for hand tracking and (ii) hand tracking in presence of an interacting object is a full-DOF problem that can be solved efficiently.
(a) the proposed method solves efficiently the continuous full-DOF hand-object tracking problem and (b) hand-object interaction is a context that facilitates full-DOF pose estimation.

the proposed method (a) solves a challenging problem of joint hand-object pose tracking based solely on marker-less multi-camera input, (b) exploits the hand-object interaction as context that facilitates hand-pose estimation and (c) is able to recover full 26-DOFs of both hands simultaneously, even when they are occluding each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for tracking the full 26-DOFs of a human hand that interacts with an object, based on markerless multi-camera input.
the development of an algorithm for full-DOF hand-object tracking that is able to cope with occlusions and physical hand-object interaction.
the problem of tracking the full pose of an interacting human hand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method can be used to estimate hand-object interactions in real time with good accuracy.

the proposed approach provides a significant improvement over the state of the art in hand-object tracking, and that the proposed approach is the first to address the full DOF tracking of the hand-object system in the presence of occlusions and physical interactions.
our approach is the first to solve the full-DOF hand-object tracking problem in a computationally efficient manner, and that it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods for isolated hands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how hand-object interaction facilitates hand pose recovery, instead of being a complicating factor.
we are able to track the hand and object together in the presence of occlusion, and we do so in an efficient manner, while the state-of-the-art can only track the isolated hand.
the proposed approach can be considered as the first to demonstrate the feasibility of tracking a human hand interacting physically with an object, based solely on marker-free multi-camera input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hand pose estimation is a much easier problem when the context of hand-object interaction is taken into account.
hand-object interaction can indeed facilitate the estimation of the hand pose.
the problem of hand pose estimation in the presence of an object can be solved efficiently by exploiting the physical constraints imposed by the interaction.
